day_shape: 78 items: US-Iran MoU rollout includes 60-day oil sales licence and disputed nuclear-inspection terms, Pentagon seeks $80B Iran war supplemental, IDF kills one near Nabatieh in Ali Taher incident, Pezeshkian lands in Islamabad, eight Iranian banks hit by outages, regime channels heavily promote Mujtaba Khamenei succession.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU implementation disputes
threads.summary: The US authorised Iran to produce and sell crude oil for 60 days under a temporary licence tied to Swiss technical talks that Tehran said concluded successfully, while Trump's claim Iran agreed to long-term nuclear inspections was denied by Tehran. Iran International reported rival readings of the memorandum across Hormuz, frozen funds, inspections, oil sanctions and Lebanon, and Iran said no plan exists for UN inspectors to visit bombed sites.

threads.label: Ali Taher incident on Lebanon border
threads.summary: The IDF said troops opened fire on four Hezbollah operatives riding a bulldozer and motorcycle near the Ali Taher ridge close to Nabatieh after they entered the security zone; Lebanese National News Agency reported one dead and two wounded near a bulldozer clearing a road. Hezbollah called it a ceasefire violation against civilians, while a fifth round of Lebanon-Israel talks began in Washington.

threads.label: Pezeshkian visit to Islamabad
threads.summary: Pezeshkian arrived in Islamabad with his aircraft escorted by six Pakistani fighters and was formally received by Shehbaz Sharif, who said he would travel to Tehran next week for the funeral of Iran's martyred leader. IRIB reported Pezeshkian saying missiles are not in the agreement and Sharif calling double standards on ballistic missiles unacceptable.

threads.label: Mujtaba Khamenei succession messaging
threads.summary: Regime and allied channels promoted Ayatollah Sayed Mujtaba Khamenei as supreme jurist, with Defa Press quoting Hezbollah's Naim Qassem saying he 'leads the front of truth' and IRIB carrying Sharif praising his leadership. Khamenei's office posted that the resistance front stands alongside Iran following the 'third imposed war', and IRGC organised media for the deceased leader's funeral procession.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz Iran-Oman alignment
threads.summary: Defa Press reported a joint Iran-Oman statement reiterating commitment to safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and Omani support for the 'Islamabad' arrangement, after lead negotiator Qalibaff returned to Tehran from consultations with Oman's Sultan and foreign minister. CENTCOM posted that USS George H.W. Bush continues operating in the Arabian Sea with two carriers in the region.

threads.label: Iran banking outages and consumer strain
threads.summary: Iran International reported at least eight Iranian banks suffered widespread service disruptions on Tuesday, with the Central Bank saying card-based service issues at Melli, Saderat and Tejarat would be resolved overnight and authorities urging cash use at petrol pumps. Iran International also reported Tehran bread prices rising up to 100% and gym fees pushing fitness out of reach.

threads.label: US war costs and Israeli posture
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported the Pentagon is seeking $80 billion from Congress for Iran war costs, that Rubio is touring Gulf states to promote the Iran deal, and that the IDF now holds roughly 70% of Gaza. Former PM Naftali Bennett said Israel had smuggled tens of thousands of Starlink receivers into Iran to aid protesters but the effort was halted under Netanyahu.

The Central Bank announced: the disruption to card-based services at all banks except Melli, Saderat and Tejarat has been resolved and the disruption to services at these three banks will also be resolved by end of tonight. The intermittent disruption that occurred at some of the country's banks, which took place to prevent any unauthorised access and protect the security of information and customers' assets, has been resolved and services at these banks have returned to normal. At present, technical teams and cybersecurity specialists are working to resolve the disruption at the systems of Melli, Saderat and Tejarat banks and the process of restoring services is continuing.

events.summary: OFPP, DoD, GSA, and NASA (collectively referred to as the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council or FAR Council) are proposing to amend the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) to implement Executive Order (E.O.) 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement. The E.O. directs the elimination of excessive acquisition regulations to stop the inefficient use of American taxpayer dollars. The FAR Council is issuing twelve proposed rules that collectively will streamline the FAR in its entirety. This rule proposes revisions to FAR parts 1, 2, 4, 33, 39, 40, 52, and 53.
